finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Checkout flow is not atomic; per-item writes & coupon race
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L420)
Evidence: Code reads coupon then updates it (coupon.findUnique -> coupon.update) and then performs multiple order/orderItem updates/creates/deletes in sequential awaits and loops without a single $transaction wrapping all related writes; individual item upserts and deletes run as separate DB writes. This allows partial commits and race conditions (coupon quantity, duplicate/partial orders) under concurrent checkouts.  
Impact: Data corruption and financial inconsistency (overspent/negative coupon counts, partial orders) that will break at small-to-moderate concurrent checkout volumes (≈50–200 concurrent checkouts).  
Fix: Wrap coupon decrement, user/create-or-update, order update/create, and all orderItems upserts/deletes in a single prisma.$transaction and batch writes (createMany/updateMany) or use transactional conditional updates to avoid per-item sequential awaits.

[DB-2] Payment confirmation decrements stock without guard
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Inside a prisma.$transaction the code blindly runs tx.product.update or tx.productColor.update with data: { stock: { decrement: item.quantity } } for each order item, with no WHERE check or conditional guard to ensure stock >= quantity.  
Impact: Overselling and negative stock values under concurrent confirmations or high-order throughput; can fail correctness at ~100+ concurrent confirmations for popular SKUs.  
Fix: Perform conditional updates (e.g., update where stock >= qty and check affected rows), or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / row-lock then validate stock inside the same transaction and fail if insufficient.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-3] Product list endpoints return unbounded result sets
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: Multiple public product endpoints (src/app/api/products/route.ts, src/app/api/products/category/[category]/route.ts, src/app/api/new-arrivals/route.ts) call prisma.product.findMany without take/limit/pagination and often include relations (colors), returning full tables.  
Impact: High-traffic list endpoints will cause full table scans and memory pressure as products grow; will degrade API latency noticeably at ~10k users and become painful by ~100k users.  
Fix: Add pagination (limit/offset or cursor), and require/validate page size; move heavy includes behind detail endpoints.

[DB-4] Missing indexes on high-traffic product filters/sorts
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L220)
Evidence: Queries frequently filter/order by category, isActive, createdAt, sortOrder and price, but the Product model lacks supporting @@index declarations on category/isActive and createdAt/sortOrder/orderable fields.  
Impact: Filters and ORDER BY on large product tables will lead to sequential scans and slow responses as table size grows (~100k+ rows), impacting all product-listing endpoints.  
Fix: Add targeted indexes (e.g., @@index([category, isActive, createdAt]) and indexes on createdAt, sortOrder, price or build composite indexes matching common query patterns).

[DB-5] Serverless DB pooling not explicitly configured
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L60)
Evidence: PrismaClient instantiated at module scope and global caching is only set for non-production, and there is no indication of an external pooler (pgbouncer) or connection-limiting config in DATABASE_URL.  
Impact: On serverless platforms each cold-started instance will open its own DB connections; without a pooler this risks exhausting Postgres connection limits at scale (hundreds of concurrent lambdas), causing outages.  
Fix: Use a serverless-safe pooler (PgBouncer), add connection-limits in DATABASE_URL or use a managed proxy, and consider enabling a production-safe global singleton pattern compatible with your deployment.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Cart APIs use transactions and indexed cart items
File: src/app/api/cart/items/route.ts (L1-L240)
Evidence: Cart add/update/delete use prisma.$transaction and schema defines multiple indexes on CartItem (cartId, [cartId, productId, selectedColor], mainCartItemId), reducing N+1 and lookup cost on cart operations.
